![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14188718/assets/e74f96531b57a877b043ac4302adae6beef90dc24d64efc8e1a24b563e4738b7.png)

Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the ellipse shown above.
question.worked_solution:
Since our ellipse is centered at $(-1,2)$ and has semiaxes $4$ and $2,$ its equation is given by

$$
\frac{(x-(-1))^{2}}{{4}^{2}}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{{2}^{2}}=1\,⟹\,\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{4}=1.
$$

Now, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{4}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{16})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{4}) & =0 \\ \frac{2(x+1)}{16}+\frac{2(y-2)}{4}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =0 \\ \frac{y-2}{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{x+1}{8} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{x+1}{4(y-2)}\end{aligned}
$$
